newsitem.title: UK: Shaftesbury buys Wereldhave's Carnaby Street.
newsitem.headline: Shaftesbury buys Wereldhave's Carnaby Street.

text.p: British property company Shaftesbury Plc said on Thursday it had agreed to buy the Carnaby Estate, covering 93 properties in and around the Carnaby Street shopping area in London's West End, for 90 million stg.

The seller is Dutch property fund Wereldhave, which made clear earlier this autumn that it was looking for buyers prepared to pay what it called "an extremely good price" for the area once famed for its swinging street-wise fashion stores.
"It is envisaged that this acquisition will be funded by a combination of debt and equity finance", Shaftesbury added in a statement, though it gave no details of any share issue plans.
Shaftesbury specialises in investment in properties in the busy retail and tourist areas in this part of central London.
Its portfolio includes shops and restaurants in Covent Garden, the Chinatown area near Leicester Square, and in Carnaby Street.
"This estate offers an outstanding opportuity for Shaftesbury to advance its proven strategy," the company added.
The statement gave not indication of Wereldhave's reasons for selling, though previous press reports have said it would want to sell for at least 69 million stg.
